correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=1, normalized perimeter arclength on the equilateral triangle gives an atomless cyclic angular measure at the centroid. A failed convex-hull capture is equivalently a single cyclic gap of at least pi (unique outside null antipodal configurations). Counting its first sample produces p_m=m E[q(X)^(m-1)]. Direct opposite-ray barycentric intersection gives Q(t)=(1-t)^2/(2-3t) on [0,1/2] and q(t)=1-Q(1-t) on [1/2,1]. A Laurent-polynomial substitution z=2-3t yields the supplied finite Q+Q log2 formula, including p_2=1 and p_3=25/27-(20/81)log2. Differentiation verifies the unique strict angular-mass maximum q(2/3)=5/9 with q''=-2; the interior Laplace estimate yields 3 sqrt(pi m/5)(5/9)^m, with strictly subleading cusp/endpoints. Independently computed m=1,2,3,4,5,10,20 integrals and a fresh 30,000-sample geometric Monte Carlo agree. The integrals, not the finite experiment, establish the all-m law.
residual_risks: Equilateral triangle only, iid normalized perimeter boundary points, all integer sample sizes; asymptotic is m->infinity. Previously known 3-point law and halfplane-mass exponent are excluded from novelty.
